correctness.rationale: The random-quantile cdf is exactly \(G(F_X(t))\); differentiating gives the exact multiplier \(u\log u\,g(u)/(G(u)\log G(u))\) between transformed and parent RAI functions. Power cdfs \(G(u)=u^a\) make this multiplier identically one. Conversely, applying universal invariance to a rate-one exponential parent makes \(u\) range over \((0,1)\), forces \(G'(u)/(G(u)\log G(u))=1/(u\log u)\), and integration gives \(G(u)=u^a\) with \(a>0\). The order and monotonic-class corollaries are immediate pointwise consequences of equality of the RAI functions. No finite experiment is used as proof.

originality.rationale: The direct 2024 source treats the same random-quantile model, but its main preservation theorem uses a common randomizer plus a usual-stochastic-order side condition. Its \(\operatorname{Beta}(n,1)\) maximum example retains that side condition, and its conclusion explicitly leaves different randomizers \(Z_1\) and \(Z_2\) for future work. The present theorem both permits different \(\operatorname{Beta}(a,1)\) and \(\operatorname{Beta}(b,1)\) randomizers without that side condition and characterizes the Beta-power family as the unique absolutely continuous universal RAI-invariant randomizers. Targeted semantic searches and two related generalized-RAI full texts did not reveal this randomizer classification.

value.rationale: The direct source singles out preservation under different randomizers as future work and, even for iid maxima, obtains only a one-way result with a usual-stochastic-order side condition. The theorem identifies a complete natural randomizer class for which the future two-randomizer problem becomes exact, removes the side condition, permits different maximum sample sizes, and proves uniqueness of that universal invariance mechanism. The result is structural rather than a numerical or parameter-slice recomputation.
